title: Surveillance on Religious Teachers Who Bypass Asatizah Recognition Scheme, and Safeguards for Minors in Mosque Activities
what_it_is: Surveillance on Religious Teachers Who Bypass Asatizah Recognition Scheme, and Safeguards for Minors in Mosque Activities

sections.label: Parliamentary questions on mosque safeguarding
sections.summary: Questions ask the Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs about unauthorised religious lessons, MUIS safeguards, background screening, and a mosque safeguarding review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim
sentences.text: asked the Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs regarding the recent case involving an individual not accredited under the Asatizah Recognition Scheme (ARS) who conducted religious lessons at a mosque (a) whether MUIS has established how he came to conduct such lessons; (b) whether similar unofficial lessons have been reported at other mosques; and (c) what safeguards is MUIS implementing to prevent such unofficial and unauthorised classes from taking place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
sentences.text: asked the Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (a) why a man recently sentenced for serious sexual offences was reportedly able to conduct religious classes in a mosque for the youth victims and their friends, despite not being a member of staff, volunteer, or an accredited religious teacher; and (b) what safeguards has MUIS implemented to ensure that only accredited asatizahs can conduct classes at mosques.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: asked the Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (a) whether mosques and Islamic education providers are required to conduct background screening on staff, volunteers and freelance instructors who work with children; (b) how many mosques have a written child safeguarding policy in place; and (c) whether MUIS will publish the findings of its current review and any resulting minimum safeguarding standards, so that parents can see what has changed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: asked the Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (a) when the review of safeguarding measures at mosques will be completed; (b) whether it will strengthen safeguards for informal religious activities involving minors, including the verification of religious teachers, supervision of adult-child interactions and access to secluded areas; and (c) whether consistent mechanisms for reporting and responding to safeguarding concerns will be established across all mosques.

sections.label: Police support for victims
sections.summary: When the case was reported to the Police in April 2024, Victim Care Officers were assigned to support the victims and their family.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: When the case was reported to the Police in April 2024, Victim Care Officers were immediately assigned by the Police to support the victims and their family.

sections.label: PELITA support for children
sections.summary: PELITA, a MUIS initiative, works with agencies and community partners to help the children with school transition, psycho-religious support and financial assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: PELITA, a MUIS initiative, has been working with agencies and community partners to help the children transition to a new school, provide psycho-religious support and offer financial assistance for their relocation and immediate needs.

sections.label: MUIS mosque safeguarding advisory
sections.summary: MUIS issued an August 2025 advisory for all mosques to strengthen safeguards for minors, including CCTV coverage and staff training.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: MUIS acted on this and issued an advisory in August 2025 to ensure that all mosques strengthened safeguards for minors, ensuring adequate closed-circuit television (CCTV) coverage and training staff to identify suspicious behaviour.

sections.label: Committee to review religious safeguards
sections.summary: A committee will be convened to review and examine safeguards across religious institutions and propose measures to strengthen them.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We can do more together, as a community.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: So, I will convene a committee to review and examine our safeguards across our religious institutions and propose measures to strengthen them.

sections.label: Committee scope and leadership
sections.summary: The committee, led by Assoc Prof Razwana Begum and Ustaz Fathurrahman Dawoed, will report to the Minister and examine safeguards and safe access to religious guidance.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The committee will report directly to me and the findings will be shared with the community.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: It will be led by two chairpersons who are respected by the community – Assoc Prof Razwana Begum and Ustaz Fathurrahman Dawoed.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: First, whether existing safeguards to protect minors, not just in our mosques but also in our religious schools, can be further strengthened.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Second, how the community, particularly children and youths, can access religious guidance safely – covering oversight of both formal and informal religious instructions and emerging risks, including online influence.

sections.label: Committee to review mosque safeguards
sections.summary: A committee will conduct a comprehensive review of safeguards in religious institutions and recommend measures to strengthen them.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We must therefore always strive to do our best for our mosques and our congregants.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: I will establish a committee to conduct a comprehensive review of the safeguards in our religious institutions, identify areas for improvements and recommend measures to strengthen existing safeguards.

sections.label: Police assessment on informing MUIS
sections.summary: Police assessed no strong public interest to disclose the offence, and no need to inform MUIS until investigations completed in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Based on the facts of the case, the Police made the assessment that there was no strong public interest to disclose the offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: In 2024, the considerations were quite a bit different because of the serious rape allegations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: And therefore, the Police moved in swiftly, arrested the individual on the same day, charged him in Court and the accused was remanded henceforth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: And as the individual had already been remanded, he was no longer an active threat to the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: And therefore, the Police made the assessment that there was no need for the Police to inform MUIS until investigations were completed, which they did in 2025.

sections.label: Police decision on informing MUIS
sections.summary: Police assessed there was no strong public interest to inform MUIS until investigations were completed in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Such information would only be available after investigations are completed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: And therefore, on balance, the Police made the decision and the assessment that there was no strong public interest to inform MUIS until investigations were completed in 2025.

sections.label: MUIS guidelines and mosque enhancements
sections.summary: Since MUIS was informed in July 2025, guidelines and two rounds of enhancements were made to strengthen safeguards at mosques.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In fact, since MUIS was informed in July 2025, there was one round, as I shared in my reply earlier, where MUIS sent out guidelines to enhance and strengthen protections for our youths and just keeping a lookout, safeguarding our mosques.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: As we knew of more of the case when the sentencing happened last month, we came up with two rounds of enhancements to our frameworks to strengthen further our mosques by putting in more guidelines, keeping a watch for gatherings involving youths and kids, also putting in CCTVs where we can, and certainly rolling out measures where we consider low-hanging fruits to maintain a certain level of assurance to parents who are concerned about the safety of their kids in our mosques.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: But at the same time, as I said, keeping that balance to keep our mosques open and welcoming.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: And that is why we have set up the review committee to look at various areas, such as how we can improve, including even cultural barriers or community settings.

sections.label: Committee to strengthen education and awareness
sections.summary: The committee will look into strengthening education, awareness, community conversations and engagement, with announcements and outputs in coming months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: But we have to overcome some of these barriers and I hope that the committee can look into how we can further strengthen education, awareness, have conversations with the community and engage them to build these new measures together as one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We will announce the committee in due course and certainly, look forward to their outputs in the coming months.

sections.label: Advisory given to 70 mosques
sections.summary: When MUIS was informed in 2025, all 70 mosques were given an advisory on measures to strengthen safeguards at mosques.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: When MUIS was informed about this case in 2025, all 70 mosques were given the advisory on measures to strengthen safeguards at mosques.

sections.label: MUIS monitoring informal youth activities
sections.summary: MUIS has tightened monitoring of informal activities involving children and youths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: MUIS has tightened the monitoring of informal activities involving children and youths.

sections.label: ARS application screening and renewal
sections.summary: Every ARS application is screened, subject to a Code of Ethics, and renewed every three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Every ARS application undergoes a screening process, is subjected to a Code of Ethics, and must be renewed every three years.

sections.label: MUIS investigates feedback and complaints
sections.summary: MUIS will investigate every feedback or complaint and may suspend or revoke an asatizah's ARS accreditation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: MUIS will investigate every feedback or complaint and take appropriate action, including suspending or revoking an asatizah's ARS accreditation.

sections.label: Certificate-based screening system considerations
sections.summary: Goh said the Government is looking into a certificate-based system, considering practicability and whether employers, mainly SMEs, can handle screening.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Goh said that the Government is looking into a certificate-based system, but considerations would include the practicability of such screening requirements and whether employers, primarily our small and medium enterprises (SMEs), will be able to handle such screening requirements.

sections.label: Children's safety priority in screening
sections.summary: Goh said children's safety takes priority, so the Government is reviewing the feasibility of implementing a screening framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: In my main reply, I have already said that while we need to strike a balance between the two, the safety of our children will have to take priority, which is why we have also committed that we are reviewing the feasibility of how to implement a screening framework.

sections.label: Screening framework implementation and consultation
sections.summary: The screening framework may add a layer to mitigate risk, but is not fool-proof, and consultation is needed for smooth implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: The screening framework that we are looking into now will provide possibly another layer for us to be able to screen and mitigate the risk against such incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: However, I just want to reiterate that it will not be a fool-proof mechanism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: In terms of how we will implement the screening framework, as I mentioned, there will be many sectors, especially many of the unregulated ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: We will have to do consultation to understand the challenges and considerations, and to make sure we are able to implement it smoothly.

sections.label: Committee appointees and community collaboration
sections.summary: Two community leaders with expertise in working with children were appointed to the committee, which aims to improve child safety in mosques and religious settings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: So, it is not purely a mosque setting or religious setting that we are looking at, but also how we can learn from this, as a community, work collaboratively with parents and community partners to improve child safety in our mosques and religious settings, as well as a wider community if we can.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: But specific to the committee, I have appointed, so far, Assoc Prof Razwana Begum and Ustaz Fathurrahman Dawoed, largely because they are both respected leaders of the community and they both have expertise working with children.

sections.label: Committee composition and publication timeline
sections.summary: The committee's composition will be announced later, and its results and outcomes are expected to be published before the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The composition of the committee will be further announced in due course.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: But I do expect the results and outcomes to be published before the end of the year.

sections.label: Review committee mandate on online risks
sections.summary: The review committee's mandate includes looking at emerging risks, including online influences on religious education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: One of the mandates that I have put into the review committee is to also look at the emerging risk, including online influences on religious education.

sections.label: Harm continued despite bail conditions
sections.summary: Despite bail conditions, the accused continued to cause harm, which stopped only in 2024 after it was reported and further harm had occurred.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: In this case, despite the bail conditions, they were all the right decisions, the accused was still able to continue to cause harm and it stopped only in 2024 after it was reported when further harm had already occurred.

sections.label: No prior reports to MUIS
sections.summary: MUIS was informed of the case only in July 2025, and records from 2021 to 2025 show no reports to MUIS about the case or perpetrator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Just to reiterate, MUIS was only informed of the case in July 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We have also checked our records between 2021 and 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: There were no reports made to MUIS at any point in time by the Mosque Board, asatizahs or any member of the public pertaining to this case or the perpetrator.

sections.label: Safeguarding measures for mosques
sections.summary: After MUIS was informed in 2025, it introduced a first set of safeguarding measures to all 70 mosques within a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Are the safeguards today or even then sufficient?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: But that is also why, in 2025, when we first informed MUIS, within a month, it came up with the first set of safeguarding measures to all our 70 mosques.

sections.label: Screening framework for ex-offenders
sections.summary: Ex-offenders face screening in public agencies and regulated sectors, but no formal framework exists for unregulated sectors, which is being looked into.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: For the offences that she has outlined and for ex-offenders who are released from those offences, in terms of regulated sectors, they would not be able to seek employment because there is an established screening framework for public agencies as well as regulated sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: However, for unregulated sectors, today, no such screening framework formally exists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Which is the reason why we have, also, in my earlier reply, said that we are looking into such a screening framework.

sections.label: Outrage of modesty cases
sections.summary: The proportion of outrage of modesty cases involving offenders known to victims has generally been stable over the last five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: The proportion of outrage of modesty cases involving offenders known to victims over the last five years generally has been stable.

sections.summary: The Minister for Social and Family Development provided a clarification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Clarification by Minister for Social and Family Development.
